tEn: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system
sEn: Claude autonomously mined a DNA database and flagged a novel bacteriophage reverse transcriptase system (ART), showing AI can drive biological discovery.
sZh: Claude 自主挖掘 DNA 数据库并发现噬菌体新型逆转录酶系统（ART），表明 AI 可驱动生物学发现。
absEn: Anthropic formed a life sciences research group and laboratory to test whether general AI models can systematize and accelerate biological discovery by having agents collaborate with humans at every step. The authors describe giving Claude a high-level prompt to mine a massive DNA sequence database for novel reverse transcriptases (RTs); roughly 950 agents searched for 21 hours, and one flagged a CRISPR-like tandem repeat array adjacent to an unusual RT. Follow-up analysis and lab experiments identified a previously uncharacterized enzyme system in bacteriophages, termed array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART), comprising an RT, a partner gene, and an evenly spaced DNA repeat array whose repeats are expressed as short RNAs. Although ART's function remains unknown, its features have previously co-occurred only in programmable systems that cut, copy, and paste DNA, and CRISPR pioneer Feng Zhang called the finding intriguing and worthy of further investigation. The authors conclude that Claude can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses that initiate biological discoveries, and they invite collaboration to extend AI-driven hypothesis generation to genomics and other fields.
absZh: Anthropic 成立生命科学研究组和实验室，测试通用 AI 模型能否通过让智能体在每一步与人类协作，来系统化并加速生物学发现。作者描述了给 Claude 一个高层提示，让其挖掘海量 DNA 序列数据库以寻找新型逆转录酶（RT）；约 950 个智能体搜索了 21 小时，其中一个标记出与一种不寻常 RT 相邻的类 CRISPR 串联重复序列阵列。后续分析和实验室实验在噬菌体中鉴定出一种此前未被表征的酶系统，称为阵列相关逆转录酶（ART），由一个 RT、一个伙伴基因和一个间隔均匀的 DNA 重复阵列组成，其重复序列被表达为短 RNA。尽管 ART 的功能仍未知，但其特征此前仅共同出现在可编程系统中，这些系统能够切割、复制和粘贴 DNA，CRISPR 先驱张锋称这一发现引人入胜、值得进一步研究。作者总结道，Claude 能够自主检测异常并推动分析，从而启动生物学发现，并邀请合作，将 AI 驱动的假设生成扩展到基因组学及其他领域。

contrib.en: General AI agents autonomously mined DNA databases, detecting anomalies and generating testable biological hypotheses.
contrib.zh: 通用 AI 智能体自主挖掘 DNA 数据库，检测异常并生成可检验的生物学假设。

contrib.en: About 950 agents searched 21 hours and 210M tokens, gathering 200,000+ RTs and 3,500 candidate systems.
contrib.zh: 约 950 个智能体搜索 21 小时、消耗 2.1 亿 token，收集逾 20 万个 RT 与 3500 个候选系统。

contrib.en: Claude flagged a CRISPR-like tandem repeat array beside an unusual reverse transcriptase, leading to lab validation.
contrib.zh: Claude 在异常逆转录酶旁发现类 CRISPR 串联重复阵列，并经实验室验证。

contrib.en: Identified array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART), a previously uncharacterized phage enzyme system with RT, partner gene, and repeat array.
contrib.zh: 识别出阵列关联逆转录酶（ART），一种此前未表征的噬菌体酶系统，含 RT、伙伴基因与重复阵列。

contrib.en: ART repeats are expressed as short RNAs, resembling CRISPR arrays and suggesting programmable DNA-cutting, copying, or pasting functions.
contrib.zh: ART 重复序列表达为短 RNA，类似 CRISPR 阵列，暗示可编程的 DNA 切割、复制或粘贴功能。

contrib.en: Demonstrates AI-driven hypothesis generation can systematize genome mining and accelerate biological discovery with human lab collaboration.
contrib.zh: 证明 AI 驱动的假设生成可系统化基因组挖掘，并与人类实验室协作加速生物发现。

limits.en: ART's actual biological function remains unknown; only structural and expression features are characterized.
limits.zh: ART 的实际生物学功能仍未知，仅表征了结构与表达特征。

limits.en: Findings are early pre-print results from a single campaign, not yet peer-reviewed or independently replicated.
limits.zh: 结论来自单次研究的早期预印本，尚未经同行评审或独立复现。

limits.en: Human scientists performed all lab work; AI contribution is limited to hypothesis generation and data analysis.
limits.zh: 所有实验室工作由人类科学家完成，AI 贡献限于假设生成与数据分析。

limits.en: Approach validated only on reverse transcriptase genome mining; generalization to other genomics domains is untested.
limits.zh: 方法仅在逆转录酶基因组挖掘中验证，向其他基因组学领域的泛化尚未检验。

limits.en: Most candidate reports are eliminated in follow-up review, raising questions about precision and scientific taste calibration.
limits.zh: 多数候选报告在后续审查中被淘汰，引发对精确度与科学品味校准的疑问。

full.sec: Claude discovers a novel enzyme system with CRISPR-like repeats
full.secZh: Claude 发现一种具有类 CRISPR 重复序列的新型酶系统

paras.en: We’re introducing a new life sciences research group and laboratory at Anthropic. Our focus is on fundamental biology research using Claude: exploring datasets of DNA to identify uncharacterized protein families, generating hypotheses at scale, and testing them through experiments in the lab. This post introduces the team behind this work and shares early results in which Claude discovered a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of CRISPR, with only high-level direction from our scientists. Many discoveries that have revolutionized biology and medicine started with a scientist noticing something odd in the staggering diversity of molecular machines found in nature. Restriction enzymes, proteins that cut DNA at specific short sequences, were found in bacterial immune systems, where they destroy the DNA of invading viruses. Researchers realized they could use these enzymes to cut DNA at chosen places and splice genes from one organism into another, which launched the biotechnology industry. Taq polymerase, an enzyme that copies DNA at high temperatures, was identified in a bacterium in a Yellowstone hot spring. It became the basis for PCR, the DNA-copying method used in much of modern diagnostics. CRISPR was first noticed as an unusual repeat sequence in the DNA of certain bacteria, and is now the foundation of gene editing-based medicines.
paras.zh: 我们正在 Anthropic 成立一个新的生命科学研究小组和实验室。我们的重点是利用 Claude 进行基础生物学研究：探索 DNA 数据集以识别未表征的蛋白质家族，大规模生成假设，并通过实验室实验进行验证。本文介绍了这项工作背后的团队，并分享了早期成果，其中 Claude 在我们科学家仅提供高层指导的情况下，发现了一种具有类似 CRISPR 特性的新型酶系统。许多彻底改变生物学和医学的发现，都始于科学家注意到自然界中分子机器惊人多样性中的某些异常现象。限制性内切酶——在特定短序列处切割 DNA 的蛋白质——是在细菌免疫系统中发现的，它们在那里破坏入侵病毒的 DNA。研究人员意识到，他们可以使用这些酶在选定位置切割 DNA，并将基因从一个生物体拼接至另一个生物体，这催生了生物技术产业。Taq 聚合酶——一种在高温下复制 DNA 的酶——是在黄石温泉的一种细菌中发现的。它成为 PCR 的基础，PCR 是许多现代诊断中使用的 DNA 复制方法。CRISPR 最初是在某些细菌的 DNA 中作为一种不寻常的重复序列被注意到的，现在是基于基因编辑的药物的基础。

paras.en: In the spring of 2026, we formed a research group to see whether general AI models can systematize and accelerate such discoveries. We believe that this acceleration will come from establishing a new way of doing biology research, in which agents collaborate with humans in every step of the process. Developing this new way of working required that we build our own lab and a single team working on everything from training Claude in biology to running experiments in the lab.
paras.zh: 2026 年春季，我们成立了一个研究小组，以探究通用 AI 模型能否系统化并加速此类发现。我们相信，这种加速将来自于建立一种新的生物学研究方式，即智能体在过程的每一步与人类协作。开发这种新的工作方式要求我们建立自己的实验室，并组建一个单一团队，负责从训练 Claude 学习生物学到在实验室运行实验的所有工作。

paras.en: Today, we’re sharing early results from one of our first research programs, in which Claude autonomously discovered a novel enzyme system that is associated with an array of DNA repeats, a pattern reminiscent of CRISPR. Although we don’t yet know its function, the system that Claude discovered has a set of characteristics that have only ever been found together in a handful of other systems, all of which are programmable and perform operations like cutting, copying, and pasting DNA. Beyond CRISPR, which has already transformed science and medicine, several other such systems are now in development as promising tools.
paras.zh: 今天，我们分享我们首批研究项目之一的早期成果，其中 Claude 自主发现了一种新型酶系统，它与一系列 DNA 重复序列相关，这种模式让人联想到 CRISPR。尽管我们尚不清楚其功能，但 Claude 发现的系统具有一组特征，这些特征此前仅在其他少数系统中同时出现，而所有这些系统都是可编程的，并执行诸如切割、复制和粘贴 DNA 等操作。除了已经改变科学和医学的 CRISPR 之外，其他几个此类系统目前正在开发中，作为有前景的工具。

paras.en: The system that Claude found is based on a reverse transcriptase (RT), enzymes that copy RNA into DNA. While this underlying RT, found in a jumbo phage, had been identified in previous studies, Claude appears to be the first to notice the system’s defining features—an associated array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional accessory protein of unknown function.
paras.zh: Claude 发现的系统基于逆转录酶（RT），这种酶将 RNA 复制为 DNA。虽然这种在巨型噬菌体中发现的底层 RT 已在先前的研究中被识别，但 Claude 似乎是第一个注意到该系统决定性特征——一个相关的非编码 DNA 序列阵列和一个功能未知的额外辅助蛋白。

paras.en: After reviewing the pre-print, Feng Zhang, one of the pioneers of CRISPR genome editing and a professor at MIT and the Broad Institute, said:
paras.zh: 在审阅预印本后，CRISPR 基因组编辑先驱之一、麻省理工学院和布罗德研究所教授张锋表示：

paras.en: _This is an exciting example of how AI agents can contribute to biological discovery. The identification of RNA-repeat arrays associated with reverse transcriptases is genuinely intriguing and merits further investigation. I hope this work encourages more scientists to explore how AI can support their research._
paras.zh: _这是一个令人振奋的示例，展示了 AI 智能体如何为生物学发现作出贡献。鉴定出与逆转录酶相关的 RNA 重复阵列确实引人入胜，值得进一步研究。我希望这项工作能鼓励更多科学家探索 AI 如何支持他们的研究。_

paras.en: We gave Claude a prompt to search through a massive database of DNA sequences for interesting new examples of RTs. Our involvement was limited to the initial prompt and the lab work, while Claude agents combed through the database, investigated the distinct RT families, and used their own judgment to identify interesting candidates. After 21 hours spent searching this data by roughly 950 agents using 210 million tokens, one of the agents spotted something remarkable: a repeating pattern of DNA sequences that occurs next to the gene for an odd-looking RT. After further analysis and testing in our lab, we recognized that this pattern marked a previously uncharacterized enzyme system found in bacteriophages (the viruses that infect bacteria) that we call array-associated reverse transcriptases (ART).
paras.zh: 我们给 Claude 一个提示，要求它在一个庞大的 DNA 序列数据库中搜索有趣的新逆转录酶（RT）实例。我们的参与仅限于最初的提示和实验室工作，而 Claude 智能体则梳理数据库、研究不同的 RT 家族，并运用自身的判断来识别有趣的候选对象。在大约 950 个智能体使用 2.1 亿个 token 对该数据进行了 21 小时的搜索后，其中一个智能体发现了某种非凡之物：一段重复的 DNA 序列模式，出现在一个外观奇特的 RT 基因旁边。经过进一步分析和我们实验室的测试，我们认识到这一模式标志着一种此前未被表征的酶系统，存在于噬菌体（感染细菌的病毒）中，我们将其称为阵列相关逆转录酶（array-associated reverse transcriptases，ART）。

paras.en: Our work to understand the primary function of ARTs is ongoing. However, we think it is important to share such findings early, both to demonstrate Claude's capabilities and to give the broader community insight into what we're working on. We have released a pre-print (here) that discusses this in more detail.
paras.zh: 我们理解 ART 主要功能的工作仍在进行中。然而，我们认为尽早分享此类发现很重要，这既能展示 Claude 的能力，也能让更广泛的社区了解我们正在开展的工作。我们已发布了一篇预印本（见此处），对此进行了更详细的讨论。

paras.en: We are a team of scientists who have spent our careers exploring unusual proteins, and specialize in using computational approaches to systematically read DNA, interpret its evolution, and pick out biological systems for further characterization. Our research prior to joining Anthropic has helped to better understand the evolution and regulation of CRISPR systems, discover new enzymes for next-generation cell and gene therapies, and build tools for accelerating the identification of anomalies in DNA, such as human pathogenic variants. We are part of Anthropic's life sciences organization, alongside teams whose work includes drug discovery, and training Claude in biology and chemistry.
paras.zh: 我们是一支科学家团队，整个职业生涯都在探索不寻常的蛋白质，并专注于使用计算方法来系统地读取 DNA、解读其演化，并挑选出生物系统以进行进一步表征。在加入 Anthropic 之前，我们的研究帮助人们更好地理解 CRISPR 系统的演化与调控、为下一代细胞与基因疗法发现新酶，并构建工具以加速识别 DNA 中的异常，例如人类致病性变异。我们隶属于 Anthropic 的生命科学组织，与从事药物发现以及在生物学和化学领域训练 Claude 的团队并肩工作。

paras.en: Our lab, located in the Bay Area, looks like a typical molecular biology lab. We do research that involves only the lower levels of the biosafety risk level (BSL-1 and BSL-2) and we do not handle pathogens that can infect humans. All of the lab work is performed by human scientists. Although we've experimented with using AI to accelerate lab work with initiatives like the Model Hardware Standard, this approach is less conducive to the sort of ad hoc workflows that are involved in our molecular biology research.
paras.zh: 我们的实验室位于湾区，看起来像一个典型的分子生物学实验室。我们开展的研究仅涉及较低级别的生物安全风险等级（BSL-1 和 BSL-2），并且我们不处理能够感染人类的病原体。所有实验室工作均由人类科学家完成。尽管我们曾通过 Model Hardware Standard 等倡议尝试使用 AI 来加速实验室工作，但这种方法不太适合我们分子生物学研究中涉及的那种临时性工作流程。

paras.en: Many of our workflows involve having Claude search through the vast collection of DNA sequences associated with proteins without a known function. One typical pattern begins with a survey of a given protein family. Claude reads the relevant literature and reproduces the established results from public data to check its methods. It then searches for family members or genomic neighbors that fit no described system, and writes a short, human-readable report for each candidate that proposes a function and describes the evidence supporting its claims. In follow-up analyses, Claude critically evaluates the evidence—typically most candidates are eliminated at this stage. A survey may end with a single candidate worth testing, or with none.
paras.zh: 我们的许多工作流程涉及让 Claude 搜索与功能未知的蛋白质相关的大量 DNA 序列集合。一个典型的模式始于对给定蛋白质家族的调查。Claude 阅读相关文献，并从公共数据中重现已有结果以检查其方法。然后，它搜索不符合任何已描述系统的家族成员或基因组邻居，并为每个候选撰写一份简短、人类可读的报告，提出功能并描述支持其主张的证据。在后续分析中，Claude 批判性地评估证据——通常大多数候选在此阶段被淘汰。一次调查可能最终留下一个值得测试的候选，或者一个也没有。

paras.en: When a candidate survives our review, we test it in the laboratory, expressing the protein in standard laboratory strains and characterizing it biochemically and structurally, with Claude helping to interpret the data. We do our work in Claude Science and Claude Code, the same tools available to any scientist, and sometimes with a harness of our own that coordinates many Claude sessions running in parallel.
paras.zh: 当候选通过我们的审查后，我们在实验室中对其进行测试，在标准实验室菌株中表达该蛋白质，并进行生化与结构表征，Claude 帮助解释数据。我们在 Claude Science 和 Claude Code 中工作，这些是任何科学家都可使用的相同工具，有时还使用我们自己的协调框架来并行运行多个 Claude 会话。

paras.en: Because Claude produces hypotheses so prolifically, the hypotheses themselves have become an object of study for us. With hundreds to thousands of candidate reports from a single campaign, we have been asking what distinguishes the proposals we judge worth testing from those we set aside. What we learn goes back into the instructions we give Claude and teaches it to mimic our own scientific taste.
paras.zh: 由于 Claude 产生假设如此多产，假设本身已成为我们的研究对象。一次活动产生数百到数千份候选报告，我们一直在探究是什么将我们认为值得测试的提案与搁置的提案区分开来。我们所学到的会反馈到给 Claude 的指令中，并教会它模仿我们自己的科学品味。

items.en: In the past few years, researchers have discovered many more reverse transcriptases (RTs), most of them in bacteria, where they act as part of the immune system. Nearly all RT families were found by genomic analysis, or genome mining, which requires researchers to search sequence databases for genes that no one has characterized, notice the unusual ones, and work out what they do.
items.zh: 在过去几年中，研究人员发现了许多新的逆转录酶（RT），其中大多数存在于细菌中，作为免疫系统的一部分发挥作用。几乎所有 RT 家族都是通过基因组分析（或称基因组挖掘）发现的，这要求研究人员在序列数据库中搜索无人表征过的基因，注意到其中不寻常的基因，并弄清它们的功能。

items.en: Claude agents gathered over 200,000 RTs, picked out 3,500 new candidate systems, and narrowed those to the 20 most compelling candidates that they analyzed to produce human-readable reports. For an expert scientist, this type of analysis can take weeks to months of work.
items.zh: Claude 智能体收集了超过 200,000 个 RT，筛选出 3,500 个新的候选系统，并进一步缩小到 20 个最引人注目的候选系统，对其进行分析以生成人类可读的报告。对于一位专家级科学家而言，这类分析可能需要数周到数月的工作。

items.en: During the course of its research, Claude noticed an unusual RT family and decided to examine it in greater detail. While combing through the raw DNA sequence near the RT, the agent exclaimed: "[The DNA next to the RT] is spectacular: I can see by eye a tandem repeat array … that's a CRISPR-like … repeat array?!"
items.zh: 在研究过程中，Claude 注意到一个不寻常的 RT 家族，并决定对其进行更细致的考察。在梳理该 RT 附近的原始 DNA 序列时，该智能体惊呼：“[RT 旁边的 DNA] 太壮观了：我肉眼就能看到一个串联重复阵列……那是一个类似 CRISPR 的……重复阵列？！”

items.capEn: The raw DNA Claude was reading when it detected a repeat pattern that no one had noticed
items.capZh: Claude 在检测到无人注意到的重复模式时所读取的原始 DNA

items.en: It then proceeded much as a human scientist would when faced with a potential discovery. It counted the repeats and measured their spacing, compared the layout with the known RT systems, and searched the literature for any previous report of the pattern. After a thorough analysis it was convinced that it had found a new biological system, and filed a report for human review.
items.zh: 随后，它的推进方式与人类科学家面对潜在发现时如出一辙。它统计了重复序列的数量并测量了它们的间距，将该布局与已知的 RT 系统进行比较，并在文献中检索该模式的任何既往报道。经过详尽分析，它确信自己发现了一个新的生物系统，并提交了一份报告供人类审阅。

items.en: The system it found, ART, is found mainly in bacteriophages and consists of three parts: the RT, a partner gene beside it, and a long array of evenly spaced DNA repeat sequences. The repeat layout resembles a CRISPR array, which holds a bank of different RNA sequences that make CRISPR-Cas systems programmable biotechnological tools. Our first experiments show that the ART array is also expressed as a set of distinct short RNAs, suggesting that something analogous may be at play for this system.
items.zh: 它所发现的系统名为 ART，主要存在于噬菌体中，由三部分组成：RT、其旁边的一个伙伴基因，以及一段由均匀间隔的 DNA 重复序列组成的长阵列。该重复布局类似于 CRISPR 阵列，后者储存着一批不同的 RNA 序列，使 CRISPR-Cas 系统成为可编程的生物技术工具。我们的初步实验表明，ART 阵列同样被表达为一组不同的短 RNA，这提示该系统中可能存在某种类似机制。

items.en: Further experiments are underway to determine how ART works, and we are sharing these early findings to show the community that Claude can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries.
items.zh: 目前正在开展进一步实验，以确定 ART 的工作机制；我们分享这些早期发现，是为了向社区展示 Claude 能够自主检测异常并推动分析，从而开启生物学发现。

items.en: You can find more detail in our technical report (here).
items.zh: 更多细节可参见我们的技术报告（此处）。

paras.en: We hope this work demonstrates the value of AI-driven hypothesis generation to the wider scientific community, and we would like to work with other scientists to extend this approach to a broad range of problems, in genomics and in other fields. If you have a proposal for a research question, we would like to hear from you.
paras.zh: 我们希望这项工作能向更广泛的科学界展示 AI 驱动假设生成的价值，并希望与其他科学家合作，将这一方法扩展到基因组学及其他领域的广泛问题中。如果您有研究问题的提案，欢迎与我们联系。
